newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Wednesday in lacklustre trade, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. February durable goods figures, which are forecast to show a decline of 0.4 percent compared with a 0.4 percent increase reported in January.

"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning following a hike in (U.S.) interest rates, the first in more than two years," a dealer said. On Tuesday, the Federal Reserve raised the Federal Fund rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.

"Everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the durable goods figures. But I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations," he said.

In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday rose 3/16 percentage point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, Thursday/Friday was unchanged from Tuesday's 6-1/8 6 percent and week-fixed eased 3/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
